method: The cut length is the finished edge multiplied by the gather ratio plus the seam allowance at both ends, so a forty inch edge at two to one with a half inch allowance needs eighty one inches of fabric. The take-up is the fabric that disappears into the gathers: the finished edge times the ratio, minus the finished edge itself, which is forty inches at two to one. The gather ratio runs from 1.1 to 4 and the page names the fullness band it falls in: below 1.5 is soft, 1.5 up to 2.5 is medium, 2.5 up to 3 is full and 3 or more is very full. Strips are counted by dividing the cut length by the usable fabric width and rounding up, so the strips can be joined end to end without a short strip at the seam; an exact fit stays one strip. The fabric per strip is the cut length divided by the strip count, which is the average strip rather than a per-strip cutting list when the last strip is short. The section plan divides both the cut length and the finished edge by the section count so the gathers can be pulled evenly between marks. Inches and centimetres are both supported; the arithmetic is unit-free and the page also shows the cut length converted at exactly 2.54 centimetres to the inch. Inputs are limited to a finished edge of 1 to 500 inches (2.5 to 1270 centimetres), a ratio of 1.1 to 4, a usable fabric width of 1 to 120 inches (2.5 to 305 centimetres), a seam allowance of 0 to 12 inches (0 to 30 centimetres) per end and 1 to 8 whole sections; text, negative numbers, exponent notation, empty fields and out of range values are refused with the field named. The page assumes a plain rectangular strip cut to the usable width with no pattern repeat, nap, directional print, selvedge or shrinkage allowance, does not model how the gather is sewn or which stitch length is used, and it stores, uploads and transmits nothing.

sources.title: Sewing and pattern-drafting practice: a gathered strip is cut at the gather ratio times the finished edge, and seam allowances are added at the ends that are joined or turned under.
Ruffle fullness guidance used in dressmaking: roughly 1.5 to 1 reads as a soft gather, 2 to 1 as a standard ruffle, and 3 to 1 or more as a dense, tutu-like gather.
Sewing construction practice: ruffles are gathered in two or more rows of long stitches and divided into equal sections so the fullness is distributed evenly along the seam.
